topic: Fundamental Constants and Mathematical Structure in Turbulence

sections.title: Prerequisites: The Language of Flux
lecture_lines: Reynolds Number measures inertia versus viscous forces.
Turbulence emerges when thresholds are exceeded.
This triggers a cascade of energy.

sections.title: The Kolmogorov Hypothesis: Self-Similarity
lecture_lines: Kolmogorov theory explains turbulent energy cascades.
Large eddies break into smaller ones.
Small scales show universal statistical behavior.
Defining the Kolmogorov length scale is crucial.
Energy is dissipated at the smallest scales.
animations: Animate large eddy splitting into smaller eddies using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/eddy.svg], #FF4500.
Highlight small scales with uniform blue, #00BFFF.

sections.title: The Mathematical Structure: The 5/3 Law
lecture_lines: The power spectrum follows the 5/3 law.
Energy scales with wavenumber to power -5/3.
The inertial subrange ignores viscous effects.
Kolmogorov constant characterizes this universal spectrum.
Turbulence follows clear, predictable mathematical laws.

sections.title: Application: Turbulence in Nature
lecture_lines: Nature uses turbulence for energy stabilization.
Falcons navigate air pockets using these dynamics.

sections.title: Summary and Conclusion
lecture_lines: Energy dissipation defines the cascade limit.
